topic: GitHub Actions script injection: pass untrusted context through env, and pin actions to a commit SHA
text:
A PR title can run code in your CI. If you paste it straight into a run: step, it does.

GitHub's hardening guide calls this script injection. Expressions like ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} are expanded before the shell runs, so the title becomes part of the script.

The fix from the docs: put the value in an intermediate environment variable, then quote it in the shell. Now it's data, not code.

Second habit from the same guide: pin third-party actions to a full-length commit SHA. Per GitHub, that's currently the only way to use an action as an immutable release. Just check the SHA comes from the official repo, not a fork.

Takeaway: never interpolate untrusted input into run:, and don't trust a movable tag.

Which CI check would you add first to catch this in code review?
